evidence.requirements: Every brief item is met. The three tastings have the exact data (store.js:6-10). The start page shows title, date and time, 'EUR n', '<n> seats left' and a 'Book <title>' link (views.js:40-46, start.jpg). The form has 'Name', 'Email' and 'Guests' (min 1, max 8) and a 'Book' button (views.js:60-63). The server rejects bookings over the seats left (app.js:43), and errors appear in the form (form.jpg). The confirmation has the heading 'Booking confirmed' plus the tasting, guests, total and reference (views.js:67-78, confirmation.jpg shows EUR 64 for 2 x 32). /staff has a 'Password' field and a 'Sign in' button, and the password comes from STAFF_PASSWORD (server.js:6, views.js:86-87). Staff see bookings grouped by tasting with name, email, guests, reference and a 'Cancel' button (views.js:91-126, staff.jpg). Cancelling frees seats because seats are computed from the stored bookings (store.js:28-31). PORT defaults to 3000 (server.js:5), the app runs on Node 22 with no dependencies, and the interface is in English. Bookings persist to data/bookings.json, which the brief allows, so the app is empty only on its first start.
evidence.correctness: Seats left are derived from live bookings, so a cancellation releases them with no counter to drift (store.js:28-31). Validation and insert run synchronously after the body await, so two concurrent requests cannot overbook (app.js:75-87, comment line 86). Guests must match /^\d+$/ and be 1..8, which rejects 2.5, 0, 9 and empty input (app.js:40). Name and email are trimmed and length-checked. File writes are atomic via tmp plus rename (store.js:21-26). References are unique (store.js:43-45). Weaknesses: a sold-out tasting still shows a 'Book' link and an open form, and only says 'Only 0 seats left' after submission (views.js:45, app.js:43). A corrupt bookings.json stops the app from starting (store.js:18-19), which is a deliberate choice but there is no recovery path. Cancelling an unknown reference silently redirects (app.js:113-116).
evidence.security: All dynamic output goes through esc(), which covers & < > " ' (views.js:1-3), and a test checks XSS escaping (test:130-141). The password check hashes both values with SHA-256 and compares them with timingSafeEqual, avoiding length leaks (app.js:59-63). The session token is 32 random bytes in a cookie set HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict (app.js:108-110). SameSite=Strict mitigates CSRF on cancel, and cancel requires a session (app.js:114). Request bodies are capped at 16 KB (app.js:25-34). Sign-in is refused when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset (app.js:103). There are no secrets in the code. Gaps: sessions never expire, there is no sign-out, the cookie has no Secure flag, sign-in has no rate limiting or lockout, and confirmation pages are open to anyone who has the 8-hex reference (but they show no personal data).
evidence.code_quality: The code is split into server.js (wiring), store.js (data), app.js (routing, validation, handlers) and views.js (HTML), about 330 lines in total. Names are clear, and validateBooking returns the first error (app.js:36-45). The routing table is compact (app.js:118-126). Error handling is central, with 413 and 500 handled separately and 500s logged (app.js:136-142). Comments are few and explain non-obvious points: concurrency (app.js:75, 86), hashing for equal lengths (app.js:60) and the corrupt-file choice (store.js:18). There is no needless abstraction.
evidence.tests: test/app.test.js has 11 integration tests on real HTTP with an isolated temp file per test. They cover: the listing with seats left and Book links; booking with confirmation total, reference and the reduced seat count; overbooking rejection at the exact boundary (8+5 rejected, 8+4 accepted); invalid name, email and guests (0, 9, 2.5, empty); unknown tasting 404; wrong password; missing STAFF_PASSWORD (503); staff grouping plus XSS escaping; cancel freeing seats; cancel without a session; and persistence across a restart. Missing: the form's labels and Book button, the confirmation's guest count, concurrent bookings, and an over-long name.
evidence.ux_design: The screenshots show an unstyled default browser look: blue underlined links, native grey buttons, small inputs and no winery branding beyond a text link (start.jpg, form.jpg). The table layout is clear and readable (start.jpg, staff.jpg). The form keeps the entered values after an error, and the error shows in red above the fields (form.jpg). The confirmation is a bare definition list with default indentation (confirmation.jpg). Missing: a sold-out state (the Book link stays at 0 seats), a confirmation step before Cancel, sign-out, and a success notice after cancelling. It works, but it feels like a prototype for a guest-facing winery site.
evidence.accessibility: The page sets html lang='en' (views.js:8), and every input is wrapped in its label element (views.js:60-62, 86). The header/main landmarks, h1/h2 hierarchy and table th headers are present. Errors use role='alert' (views.js:5), and #a00 on white has sufficient contrast. Gaps: errors are not tied to their fields (no aria-invalid or aria-describedby) and focus does not move to them. Every Cancel button has the same accessible name with no booking context (views.js:101, staff.jpg). The action column header is empty (views.js:36, 112). The tables have no caption, and the focus styles are only the browser defaults.
evidence.simplicity: There are zero runtime dependencies (package.json): node:http, node:crypto, node:fs and node:test only. A plain JSON file serves as the store, and the whole app is small and right-sized, with no framework or build step.

strengths: Correct seat accounting that holds under concurrency: seats are derived from stored bookings, and validation plus insert run with no await in between (store.js:28-31, app.js:75-87). A test checks the exact over-booking boundary.

Solid security basics: every output is escaped, the password is compared with a hash and timingSafeEqual, the session token is random in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, request bodies are capped, and sign-in is refused when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset.
Small, dependency-free and well-structured code (store, app, views), with meaningful HTTP integration tests that cover nearly every requirement in the brief.
issues: The guest-facing design is the browser default with no winery branding (start.jpg, form.jpg, confirmation.jpg). A sold-out tasting still offers a Book link and form and only fails after submission (views.js:45).

Staff sessions never expire and cannot be ended: there is no sign-out, no Secure cookie flag and no rate limiting on sign-in (app.js:48, 108-110). Cancel takes effect immediately with no confirmation step.

Accessibility gaps: errors are not tied to their fields with aria-invalid or aria-describedby, all Cancel buttons share the same accessible name, and some table header cells are empty (views.js:5, 36, 101, 112).
review.verdict: The app meets every requirement in the brief, has sound seat logic and reasonable security, and comes with meaningful tests in a small dependency-free codebase. Before it goes to the winery's guests it needs a visual pass, a proper sold-out state, staff sign-out and session expiry, and better links between errors and fields.
